questions.q: A design specification
o: lists the requirements a product must meet
questions.why: It's written after research and used to evaluate.

questions.q: Anthropometrics is
o: the study of human body measurements for design
questions.why: Ergonomics uses this data.

questions.q: Why is a design brief written?
o: To state the problem, the user and the context clearly
questions.why: The specification then turns it into measurable points.

questions.q: Which is the best specification point for a child's lunchbox?
o: It must hold a 500 ml drinks bottle and weigh less than 300 g when empty.
questions.why: A good specification point is measurable, so the final product can be tested against it. 'Nice', 'good quality' and 'like it' cannot be checked objectively.

questions.q: When sizing a chair for adults, why does a designer often use the 5th to 95th percentile of body measurements?
o: Because it is the size of the average person
Because it covers only the tallest users
To reduce the cost of materials
So the chair suits the large majority of users, not just one average size
questions.why: Designing between the 5th and 95th percentiles accommodates about 90% of the population. Designing for the average alone would suit few people well.

long.q: Explain why a designer would write a specification before producing ideas.
scheme: B1: it sets measurable requirements (function, size, cost, users)
B1: ideas can be judged against it
B1: the final product is evaluated against it

long.q: A designer is developing a new school bag for students aged 11–16. Describe three different methods the designer could use to research the needs of the users.
scheme: B1: a questionnaire or interviews with students, e.g. asking what they carry and what they dislike about current bags
B1: product analysis of existing bags, e.g. comparing capacity, straps, materials and price
B1: a third, different method, e.g. observing students carrying bags; weighing a typical day's load; looking up anthropometric data for back length and shoulder width

long.q: Explain the difference between a design brief and a design specification.
scheme: B1: a design brief is a short statement of the problem and what is to be designed, and for whom
B1: a specification is a detailed list of measurable requirements the product must meet, written after research and used to judge ideas

long.q: A designer is planning a chair for children aged 6–10. Explain how anthropometric data would be used to decide (a) the seat height and (b) the width of the seat.
scheme: B1: anthropometric data gives body measurements for the user group, e.g. lower-leg length and hip width of children aged 6–10
B1: (a) seat height is based on the smaller users (around the 5th percentile lower-leg length) so their feet reach the floor
B1: (b) seat width is based on the larger users (around the 95th percentile hip width) so they fit comfortably
B1: designing between the 5th and 95th percentiles suits about 90% of the user group

long.q: Before making a phone stand in acrylic, a designer makes a model from card and foam board. Explain two reasons for modelling a design before making the final product.
scheme: B1: to test the design, e.g. check the angle, stability and that the phone fits
B1: explained: faults are found and corrected before expensive material and time are used
B1: to show the design to the client or users
B1: explained: their feedback can be used to improve the design before it is finalised

questions.q: Which is a thermoplastic?
questions.why: Thermoplastics can be reheated and reshaped.

questions.q: A hardwood comes from
questions.why: e.g. oak, beech.

questions.q: An alloy is
o: a mixture of a metal with other elements
questions.why: e.g. brass (copper and zinc).

questions.q: Which properties make copper suitable for electrical wiring?
o: It softens when heated and can be remoulded
questions.why: Copper conducts electricity very well and is ductile, so it can be drawn into thin wire. It is not magnetic or brittle.

questions.q: MDF (medium-density fibreboard) is
o: a manufactured board made from wood fibres and resin, with a smooth, stable surface
a dense hardwood from tropical forests
an aluminium alloy used for casting
a thermosetting plastic used for plug sockets
questions.why: MDF is a manufactured board of compressed wood fibres bonded with resin. It has no grain, is stable and takes paint well, but it is not a natural timber.

long.q: A child's toy is to be made from beech. Give two reasons why beech is suitable and one finish you would apply.
scheme: B1: close grain, so it can be shaped and smoothed well
B1: hard and durable, so it survives rough use
B1: a non-toxic finish, e.g. food-safe oil or water-based varnish

long.q: Explain the difference between hardwoods and softwoods, and give one example of each.
scheme: B1: hardwoods come from broad-leaved (mostly deciduous) trees; softwoods come from coniferous trees
B1: hardwoods grow more slowly, so they are usually more expensive; softwoods grow quickly and are cheaper
B1: a correct hardwood, e.g. oak, beech, ash, mahogany, teak
B1: a correct softwood, e.g. pine, spruce, cedar, larch

long.q: Flat-pack bookshelves are often made from veneered MDF instead of solid pine. Give two advantages and one disadvantage of MDF for this product.
scheme: B1: available in large, flat, stable boards that don't warp, twist or split
B1: a second advantage, e.g. cheaper than solid timber; smooth surface takes veneer or paint well; uses waste wood fibres
B1: a disadvantage, e.g. swells and weakens if it gets wet; screws hold poorly in its edges; heavy; dust is harmful when cut

long.q: Copper is used for domestic water pipes. (a) Explain why copper is described as a non-ferrous metal. (b) Give two properties that make copper suitable for water pipes. (c) Brass is an alloy. State what an alloy is and name the two main metals in brass.
scheme: B1: (a) it contains no iron
B1: (b) resists corrosion, so it won't rust in water
B1: (b) a second property, e.g. ductile and malleable, so it can be bent and formed; easy to join by soldering; good thermal conductor for heating pipes
B1: (c) an alloy is a mixture of a metal with one or more other elements
B1: (c) brass is copper and zinc

long.q: Explain what is meant by a smart material, and describe how a thermochromic pigment could make a baby's feeding spoon safer.
scheme: B1: a smart material changes one of its properties in response to a change in its surroundings (e.g. temperature, light) and reverses when the change is removed
B1: thermochromic pigment changes colour at a set temperature
B1: the spoon changes colour if the food is too hot, warning the parent before feeding the baby

questions.q: Injection moulding is best suited to
o: mass production of identical plastic parts
questions.why: High setup cost, very low unit cost.

questions.q: A jig is used to
o: guide a tool so parts are made accurately and repeatably
questions.why: Useful in batch production.

questions.q: Which process is used to shape thin thermoplastic sheet over a mould?
questions.why: Heat the sheet, then the vacuum pulls it over the mould.

questions.q: Which process is most suitable for making hollow plastic drinks bottles in large numbers?
questions.why: Blow moulding inflates a heated plastic tube (parison) against a mould to form a hollow shape, and it is fast enough for mass production.

questions.q: Which joint is a strong, traditional choice for joining a wooden table leg to a rail?
questions.why: A mortise and tenon gives a large gluing area and resists racking, which suits leg-and-rail frames. Butt joints are weak, pop rivets join sheet metal, and comb joints suit box corners.

long.q: A school workshop must make 30 identical pine boxes. (a) Explain two benefits of using a jig or template for marking out and drilling the parts. (b) Name a suitable corner joint for the boxes and give one reason for your choice.
scheme: B1: (a) every part is identical and accurate, so quality is consistent
B1: (a) faster: no need to measure and mark out each piece
B1: (b) a suitable joint, e.g. comb (finger), lap (rebate) or dowel joint
B1: (b) a matching reason, e.g. a comb joint's large gluing area makes it strong; dowel holes are quick to drill with a jig

long.q: Describe how a 3 mm acrylic sheet can be bent to make a 90° bend for a phone stand using a strip heater. Include one safety precaution.
scheme: B1: mark the bend line (with a chinagraph pencil or on the protective film) and place the line over the heating element
B1: heat evenly, turning the sheet over regularly, until it softens along the line
B1: bend it over a former or in a bending jig and hold it until it cools and sets at 90°
B1: a precaution, e.g. wear heat-resistant gloves; don't overheat, as acrylic blisters and gives off fumes; use in a ventilated area

long.q: Explain the difference between one-off production and batch production, giving an example of a product made by each method.
scheme: B1: one-off: a single product made to a customer's individual requirements, usually by skilled workers
B1: a correct example, e.g. a made-to-measure kitchen, a theatre set, a prototype
B1: batch: a set number of identical products made together, then the equipment is changed for the next batch
B1: a correct example, e.g. bread in a bakery, school furniture, seasonal clothing ranges

long.q: Describe the main stages of sand casting an aluminium bracket.
scheme: B1: a wooden pattern of the bracket is made, slightly oversize (to allow for shrinkage) and with tapered sides (draft)
B1: the pattern is placed in the drag (lower box) and casting sand is rammed around it; the cope (top box) is added with sprue and riser pins
B1: the pattern and pins are removed, leaving a cavity, runner and riser
B1: molten aluminium is poured into the sprue until it rises in the riser
B1: after cooling the sand is broken away and the casting is fettled (sprue and riser cut off, edges filed)

long.q: Describe how to solder a resistor to a printed circuit board (PCB) to make a good joint, and give one safety precaution.
scheme: B1: bend the leads, push the resistor through the holes on the component side and bend the leads slightly so it stays in place
B1: heat the copper pad and the lead together with the soldering iron tip
B1: feed solder onto the pad and lead (not the iron) until it flows into a small cone shape, then remove solder and iron; trim the excess lead
B1: a precaution, e.g. return the iron to its stand; use fume extraction; wear eye protection when trimming leads

questions.q: Designing for disassembly helps
o: recycling and repair at the end of a product's life
questions.why: Part of the circular economy.

questions.q: Which material is most sustainable for a disposable product?
questions.why: Consider the whole life cycle.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of product analysis?
o: To find out how and why an existing product was designed and made
questions.why: Consider function, materials, manufacture, user and sustainability.

questions.q: Which of the 6 Rs means designing a product so it can be mended rather than thrown away?
questions.why: Repair keeps products in use for longer, for example by using replaceable parts and standard fixings. Reduce is about using less material, Rethink is about redesigning the approach, and Refuse is about not using something at all.

questions.q: Planned obsolescence means
o: designing a product to last as long as possible
recycling old products into new ones
planning how a product will be packaged
designing a product so it becomes out of date or stops working after a certain time
questions.why: Planned obsolescence encourages people to replace products sooner, which raises sales but increases waste and resource use.

long.q: Explain how a designer could make an electric kettle more sustainable. Give two design changes and say how each one helps.
scheme: B1: a change, e.g. recycled or recyclable plastic marked with its recycling code
B1: explained, e.g. less new material used; easy to sort at end of life
B1: a second change, e.g. screws not glue so it can be taken apart; a replaceable element; better insulation
B1: explained, e.g. parts can be repaired or separated for recycling; less energy used to reboil

long.q: Explain what is meant by 'reduce' and 'repair' in the 6Rs, and describe how each could be applied to the design of a mobile phone.
scheme: B1: reduce: use less material and energy in making and using the product
B1: applied, e.g. a smaller, lighter case; less packaging; a more energy-efficient battery and screen
B1: repair: the product can be mended rather than thrown away
B1: applied, e.g. a battery and screen that can be replaced with standard screws, and spare parts made available

long.q: A garden bench is to be made from hardwood. (a) Explain why the designer should choose timber certified by the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC). (b) Give two design features that would make the bench last longer outdoors.
scheme: B1: (a) FSC timber comes from forests that are managed sustainably
B1: (a) trees felled are replaced, protecting habitats and the long-term timber supply
B1: (b) a feature, e.g. a durable outdoor timber such as teak or iroko, or an exterior preservative or oil finish
B1: (b) a second feature, e.g. stainless steel or galvanised fixings that won't rust; gaps between slats so rainwater drains; feet that keep the end grain off wet ground

long.q: Explain two ways the packaging for a box of chocolates could be redesigned to reduce its impact on the environment.
scheme: B1: a change, e.g. replace the plastic tray with a moulded pulp or card insert
B1: explained, e.g. it is made from recycled material and can be recycled or composted
B1: a second change, e.g. remove the separate outer sleeve or plastic film; reduce the box size to fit the contents
B1: explained, e.g. less material is used and more boxes fit in each lorry, so transport energy falls

long.q: Compare a disposable plastic razor with a metal safety razor that uses replaceable blades, in terms of cost to the user and environmental impact.
scheme: B1: disposable razor is cheaper to buy at the start
B1: safety razor costs more initially, but replacement blades are cheap, so it can be cheaper over time
B1: disposable razors produce much more waste: the whole mixed-material razor goes to landfill
B1: the metal safety razor lasts for years and only the small steel blade is replaced, which can be recycled

questions.q: An exploded drawing shows
questions.why: Parts are drawn spaced along their assembly lines.

questions.q: Orthographic projection shows
o: front, side and plan views to scale
questions.why: Used for manufacturing drawings.

questions.q: What is an exploded drawing used for?
o: To show the colour scheme only
To show how parts fit together
questions.why: Parts are drawn apart along assembly lines.

questions.q: On an orthographic drawing, what does a thin chain line (long and short dashes) show?
questions.why: Thin chain lines mark centre lines, for example through holes. Hidden detail uses thin dashed lines, and outlines use thick continuous lines.

questions.q: Which drawing method shows vertical edges as vertical and horizontal edges at 30° to the horizontal?
questions.why: Isometric drawing uses 30° lines for horizontal edges. Oblique keeps the front face true and draws depth at 45°, and orthographic shows flat views.

long.q: Explain why a manufacturer would want a dimensioned orthographic drawing of a product rather than a 3D sketch.
scheme: B1: each view shows the true shape and size, with no distortion
B1: it can be fully dimensioned to drawing standards, so parts are made accurately
B1: the conventions are understood by any manufacturer, so there's no ambiguity

long.q: State two differences between isometric projection and oblique projection.
scheme: B1: in isometric, the receding lines are drawn at 30° to the horizontal on both sides; in oblique, the front face is drawn flat and the receding lines are at 45°

B1: in oblique, the front face shows its true shape (so circles stay circles), and the depth is often halved; in isometric no face shows its true shape and all lengths along the axes are drawn full size

long.q: A drawing of a toy is drawn to a scale of 1:5. (a) On the drawing, the length of the toy is 64 mm. Calculate its real length. (b) The real height of the toy is 450 mm. Calculate its height on the drawing.
scheme: M1: (a) real length = 64 × 5

long.q: Describe how rendering can be used on a sketch to show (a) that a surface is curved and (b) that a material is transparent, such as a clear acrylic cover.
scheme: B1: (a) tone graded gradually from light to dark across the curve
B1: (a) a highlight (white strip) left along the part nearest the light source
B1: (b) lines or edges behind the part are drawn so they can be seen through it
B1: (b) a few diagonal white streaks or reflections, with only light colour or tone

long.q: A designer draws a net (development) for a card box. Explain how the drawing shows the difference between cut lines, fold lines and glue tabs, and give one reason glue tabs are needed.
scheme: B1: cut lines are drawn as continuous (solid) lines
B1: fold lines are drawn as dashed or chain lines (and scored before folding)
B1: glue tabs are drawn as tapered flaps on the edges that join, often shaded or labelled
B1: tabs give an overlapping area for glue so the box holds together with a strong, neat joint

questions.q: A potential divider with an LDR can be used to
o: switch on a light when it gets dark
questions.why: The LDR's resistance rises in the dark.

questions.q: A cam converts
questions.why: The follower rises and falls.

questions.q: In a circuit, what does an LDR do?
o: It switches at a set temperature
Its resistance changes with light level
questions.why: Used as a light sensor in a potential divider.

questions.q: In a wheelbarrow, a second-class lever, where is the load?
o: Beyond the effort, at the far end of the handles
Between the fulcrum and the effort
There is no load in a second-class lever
questions.why: In a second-class lever the load sits between the fulcrum (the wheel) and the effort (the handles), which gives a mechanical advantage greater than 1.

questions.q: A driver gear with 20 teeth turns a driven gear with 60 teeth. What is the velocity ratio (driven teeth ÷ driver teeth)?
questions.why: 60 ÷ 20 = 3, so the driven gear turns three times slower than the driver (and with more torque). Subtracting or adding the teeth is a common mistake.

long.q: A potential divider has a 9 V supply, R1 = 10 kΩ at the top and R2 = 5 kΩ at the bottom. (a) Calculate the output voltage across R2, showing your working. (b) R2 is replaced by an LDR. Explain what happens to the output voltage as it gets darker.
scheme: M1: Vout = Vin × R2 ÷ (R1 + R2)
A1: 3 V (with the unit)
B1: (b) the LDR's resistance increases as light falls
B1: (b) so it takes a bigger share of the supply and Vout rises
long.ans: (a) 3 V; (b) Vout rises as it gets darker

long.q: An LED is to be powered from a 9 V battery. The LED needs 2 V across it and a current of 20 mA. (a) Calculate the value of the series resistor. (b) Resistors come in preferred values, including 330 Ω and 390 Ω. Which would you choose, and why?
scheme: M1: (a) voltage across the resistor = 9 − 2 = 7 V
B1: (b) 390 Ω: the next value above, so the current stays slightly below 20 mA and the LED is not over-driven

long.q: A first-class lever has an effort of 50 N applied 600 mm from the fulcrum. The load is 150 mm from the fulcrum on the other side. (a) Calculate the load that can be balanced. (b) Calculate the mechanical advantage.
scheme: M1: (a) moments: load × 150 = 50 × 600
A1: (a) load = 200 N
M1: (b) MA = load ÷ effort = 200 ÷ 50

long.q: Explain the difference between a frame structure and a shell structure, giving an example of each, and explain how triangulation makes a frame structure stronger.
scheme: B1: a frame structure is made of members joined together, e.g. a bicycle frame, a pylon, roof trusses
B1: a shell structure is a thin outer surface that encloses a space and carries the load, e.g. an egg, a car body, a drinks can
B1: a rectangular frame can be pushed out of shape (it is not rigid)
B1: adding a diagonal member makes triangles, which cannot change shape without a member changing length, so the frame stays rigid

long.q: In a fan control circuit, a temperature sensor cannot supply enough current to run the motor, so a transistor is used. (a) Explain the job of the transistor. (b) Explain why a diode is connected across the motor.
scheme: B1: (a) the transistor acts as an electronic switch
B1: (a) a small current into the base from the sensor circuit switches on a much larger collector current through the motor
B1: (b) when the motor switches off, its coil produces a large reverse voltage (back e.m.f.)
B1: (b) the diode gives this a safe path, protecting the transistor from damage

questions.q: The project folio should show
o: research, ideas, development, making and evaluation
questions.why: Every stage of the design process is marked.

questions.q: In coursework, what does good development show?
o: Ideas improved through models, tests and feedback
questions.why: Explain each decision.

questions.q: What should testing the final product check?
questions.why: Use users and measurements as evidence.

questions.q: Why should a folio include a production plan before making begins?
o: To organise the order of tasks, tools, equipment and quality checks
Because it is the only section that is marked
To show the final colour scheme
questions.why: A production plan sequences the making stages and quality-control checks so that the product is made efficiently and accurately.

questions.q: Which is the most useful evaluation statement?
o: It took me a long time to finish.
Five users tested it and three found the handle too narrow, so I would widen it to 35 mm to meet specification point 4.
questions.why: A good evaluation uses evidence from testing, refers to the specification and suggests a specific improvement. The others are vague or irrelevant.
